items.title: RPC: DeepSeek V4 output degenerates to a repeated token with two RPC workers after a long prompt, and the slot stays corrupted
items.author: bobsummerwill
items.body_excerpt:
### Name and Version

`llama-server` built from 42c787e8c (2026-10-07) on all three hosts, `-DGGML_RPC=ON`.

### Operating systems

Linux (main host, one RPC worker), macOS (one RPC worker)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server, RPC backend (`ggml-rpc-server`)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

With DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (unsloth `UD-IQ4_XS` GGUF, `deepseek4` arch) split across the main host
and **two** RPC workers, a long prompt (~18k tokens) returns the same token over and over
(`DDDDDDDD…`, token id 38). The slot that processed it then stays broken: every later request
served from that slot, short ones included, returns the same repeated token, and requests with a
grammar (tools, `response_format`) fail with `Unexpected empty grammar stack after accepting piece:
D (38)`. Requests served by the other slot are fine. The same build, model, flags and requests
give correct output with no RPC, or with either RPC worker alone.

**Setup** (1 GbE LAN, ~0.3–0.6 ms between hosts)

| host | role | hardware | build |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `llama-server` | 2× RTX 3090 (sm_86, driver 595.84), Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 62 GB, Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0 | CUDA 12.6, `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_CUDA_NCCL=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` |
| B | `ggml-rpc-server -H <ip> -p 50052 -d CUDA0 -c` | RTX 5070 12 GB (sm_120, driver 580.178.04), Ubuntu 24.04 | CUDA 12.8, `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120` |
| C | `ggml-rpc-server -H <ip> -p 50052 -d MTL0 -c` | Mac mini M4 Pro 64 GB, macOS 27.0.1 | Metal (default) |

**Server command (host A)**

```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00004.gguf \
  --rpc <B>:50052,<C>:50052 --fit on --fit-target 1024 --ctx-size 65536 --parallel 2 \
  --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 512 --flash-attn on --jinja --reasoning-format deepseek \
  --reasoning off --temp 0.7 --top-p 0.95
```

**Reproducer:** `dsv4_rpc_repro.py` in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/bobsummerwill/8010490af0fb6d55875a51389e6f5ae3) (Python standard library only). It sends, at
temperature 0 with thinking disabled: a warm-up and three short prompts; a ~18k-token prompt built
from `llama.cpp/src/*.cpp`; two concurrent 300-token requests; twelve OpenAI-style tool-calling
requests (`--short`: one); and three times a short "reply with exactly SHADOWFAX-EXACT-7" probe.

```
python3 dsv4_rpc_repro.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --llama-src /path/to/llama.cpp [--short]
```

**Results** (fresh server for each row; full client logs in the [gist](https://gist.github.com/bobsummerwill/8010490af0fb6d55875a51389e6f5ae3))

| RPC workers | sequence | degenerate replies |
|---|---|---|
| B + C | full | **`prefill_16k`, `concurrent_2`, `tool:error_recovery`, `exact_1..3`** |
| B + C | short | **`prefill_16k`, `concurrent_2`, `exact_1..3`** |
| none (host A only) | full | none |

Earlier runs of the same sequence through our benchmark harness: corrupted with B + C (2 of 2
runs), clean with B only, C only, and none (1 run each). With B + C but without the long prompt
first, the tool-call and probe requests were all correct (2 runs).

**Observations**
- The first bad reply is the long prompt itself. Afterwards, every request served by that slot
  degenerates, even after its cache is cut back to 1 token (`cached_tokens: 1`) or reused (18
  tokens). The other slot keeps answering correctly (`concurrent_1`, most tool calls).
- Throughput looks normal (no crash, no RPC error in the server log at default verbosity).
- Either worker alone is fine, so this does not look like a CUDA-on-sm_120 or Metal kernel
  problem by itself, but like state that goes wrong only with two RPC workers. Possibly related
  to #28047 (split scheduler shipping views to the wrong RPC worker with >= 2 workers, also
  reproduced with deepseek4), which crashed rather than corrupting output; this build includes
  its fix.
- Not tried yet: other models, a single host with two `ggml-rpc-server` processes, or which part
  of the prompt length triggers it.

### First Bad Commit

Unknown (only 42c787e8c tested).

### Relevant log output

```
DEGENERATE prefill_16k              prompt=18455 cached=0  276.1s  :: 'DDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDD…'
ok         concurrent_1             prompt=20 cached=0   37.2s  :: '**TCP Congestion Control: Variant 1 (Tahoe)**…'
DEGENERATE concurrent_2             prompt=20 cached=0   37.2s  :: 'DDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDD…'
DEGENERATE tool:error_recovery      prompt=907 cached=1  138.4s  :: 'DDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDD…'
DEGENERATE exact_1                  prompt=22 cached=1    4.0s  :: 'DDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDD…'

server: got exception: Unexpected empty grammar stack after accepting piece: D (38)
```

items.title: Should LMCacheMPConnector honor kv_transfer_config.kv_role — or is MP mode intentionally always-kv_both?
items.author: kezboard233
items.body_excerpt:
## Context

We run a production-shaped POC on 8×V100 (two vLLM TP4 instances of Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 sharing one LMCache MP server with a CPU L1 tier) and filed #5143 with a runtime-verified repro: an engine launched with `kv_role="kv_consumer"` still stores every request's KV into the shared L1 — a single 32K-token cold request produced `168 × "Stored 784"` lines (= full prefix × 4 TP ranks), and the only engine that received any request in that window was the `kv_consumer` one.

We later found #4665 (closed by its author without maintainer response) reporting the same mechanism from the CacheBlend angle: the single-process connector honors `kv_role` / `skip_save`, the MP connector honors neither. As of today's `dev`, `lmcache_mp_connector.py` still contains no occurrence of `kv_role` / `kv_consumer` / `kv_producer` / `force_skip_save`.

## The design question

Before we contribute a patch, we want to check intent: **is MP mode intentionally "every connected engine writes"?** Two readings:

1. **Contract gap** — vLLM makes `kv_role` mandatory, documents it as "Whether this vLLM instance produces, consumes KV cache, or both", and exposes `is_kv_producer` / `is_kv_consumer` for connectors to branch on; LMCache's own single-process adapter honors it (`force_skip_save` in `vllm_v1_adapter.py`). Under this reading we'd gladly contribute a small PR that skips store-metadata generation when `is_kv_consumer` (mirroring the single-process gate), so warm-then-read-only fleets and PD-style topologies become possible on the MP path.

2. **Intentional always-kv_both** — the MP tier is a shared scratch space where every connected engine contributes. Under this reading we'd instead ask for the intent to be documented, plus ideally a one-line warning at connector init when `kv_role != "kv_both"`, so users aren't misled (we only noticed via instrumented counter evidence ourselves).

Happy to do either — a steer from maintainers decides which.

(Impact context: no correctness issue — stored content is identical — but a consumer-role engine burns D2H bandwidth and shared-L1 capacity; a 32K prefix on our model is ≈8.6 GB across 4 ranks.)

items.title: [Bug]: Grouped MLA generation cubins are registered as Dense in kernelMetaInfo.h but named and selected as Causal
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

TensorRT-LLM main, `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/trtllmGenKernels/fmha/cubin/kernelMetaInfo.h` (artifacts from #19591). On release/1.3 the table is split per architecture since #20022; the same rows are in `kernelMetaInfoSm100f.h` and `kernelMetaInfoSm107.h` (see the location list below). Seen on SM107; the SM100f rows have the same pattern.

### Who can help?

@pengbowang-nv @farazkh80 (#15009)

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Reproduction

All 36 grouped MLA generation cubins (`fmhaSm100fKernel_...` and `fmhaSm107aKernel_Qkv{Bfloat16,E4m3}OBfloat16HQk576HV512{,HVPerCta128,HVPerCta256}PagedKvCausalP32...VarSeqQ64Kv128{Static,Persistent}GroupedKeepsAbForGen`; per architecture 9 with BF16 and 9 with E4M3 Q/KV, 18 for `kSM_100f`, 18 for `kSM_107`) have `Causal` in the function name, but their `mMaskType` field is `0` (`TrtllmGenAttentionMaskType::Dense`). Locations:

- main @ 13e19d6cf3, `kernelMetaInfo.h`: SM100f BF16 lines 19057-19110, SM100f E4M3 19347-19400, SM107 BF16 20903-21019, SM107 E4M3 21907-22023.
- release/1.3 @ c9d1169641 (after #20022): `kernelMetaInfoSm100f.h` lines 243-296 (BF16) and 533-586 (E4M3); `kernelMetaInfoSm107.h` lines 887-1003 (BF16) and 1835-1951 (E4M3). The values are unchanged by the split. The grouped P128 E4M3 H128 cubins added there for SM107 are registered with `mMaskType = 1` (Causal), so only the HQk576 grouped MLA rows are affected.

`mMaskType` is part of the hash that the cubin path looks up (`hashFromFmhaOptions` -> `hashID`). With `FmhaOptions::mSelectsGroupedMla = true`, the autotuner selects the grouped kernel with a causal mask for MLA generation with multiple query tokens, so the lookup fails (`Trtllm-gen kernels not found`), and the only remaining route is NVRTC. On SM107, NVRTC currently fails for these configurations (separate issue). We had to map Causal back to Dense for grouped MLA kernels in `algoFilterForCubinPath` before the cubins could be used.

With that mapping, the cubins give the expected causal result: compared with the non-grouped kernel on SM107, outputs are bit-identical for KV lengths 16 and 64, and at most 2 bf16 ulp apart from 256 up to 128K. So the kernels behave as their names say, and only the metadata is off. #15009 also mentions that its re-exported rows were changed to `maskType=Causal` "to match the shipped lib's grouped mask rewrite".

### Expected behavior

The registered mask type matches what the kernel implements and what the selector asks for, so that grouped MLA generation cubins can be found without a remapping.

### actual behavior

`mMaskType = Dense` for kernels named `...Causal...`; the cubin lookup misses them when grouped MLA selection is enabled.

### additional notes

This does not affect main today because `mSelectsGroupedMla` is never set in TensorRT-LLM. It blocks enabling it (#15009), together with the missing `cumSeqLensQ/Kv` in the MLA generation path (#20375). If the right fix is on the export side, a regenerated `kernelMetaInfo.h` (`kernelMetaInfoSm100f.h` / `kernelMetaInfoSm107.h` after #20022) would be enough; otherwise I can send the remapping as a small PR.

Related: #20375, #20377, #20382 (FP8-KV grouped MLA hang for head counts that do not divide 64).

items.title: [Performance]: DFlash prefill context store blocks on a D2H read at every chunk, idling the GPU between chunks
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

With a DFlash drafter bound to the draft KV cache manager, `DFlashWorker._store_prefill_context` (`tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/dflash.py`) reads the context rows' draft page counts with `(self._ctx_block_counts[:num_contexts] * page_size).tolist()` at the end of every context forward. `_ctx_block_counts` is filled on the GPU earlier in the same forward, so this `.tolist()` waits for the whole forward's GPU work. The executor's host work between chunks (resource update, scheduling, input preparation) then cannot overlap the next chunk, and with chunked prefill the GPU idles at every chunk boundary.

Measured on Rubin, TP8 across 2 nodes (MNNVL), Kimi K3 with a DFlash-style drafter, 128K prompt with chunked prefill: about 11 ms of GPU idle at every chunk boundary, and the `.tolist()` itself blocks for up to about 190 ms (the rest of the forward).

Proposal: the page counts are a function of `draft_kv_cache_block_offsets`, which `attn_metadata.prepare()` fills before the forward is enqueued. Compute them in `DFlashSpecMetadata.prepare()` with the same formula on the same tensor, copy them non-blocking into pinned memory behind an event, and let `_store_prefill_context` use that snapshot (waiting only on the event, which completes when the forward starts). Fall back to the current read whenever the snapshot does not match the forward (different tensor, row count, manager or pool). Opt-in first via `TLLM_DFLASH_PREFILL_CTX_SNAPSHOT=1`. With it, 128K TTFT dropped by about 0.36 s in the setup above. PR to follow.

items.title: [Performance]: Kimi KDA verify runs the qkvg and [f_a | b] projections as two GEMMs on two streams
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

In the Kimi KDA mixer's MTP verify (`KimiKDALinearAttention._project_verify_inputs`, `tensorrt_llm/_torch/modules/kimi_kda/kimi_kda_mixer.py`), the BF16 full-rank-gate path runs two GEMMs on the same input: the fused `[q | k | v | g]` projection (`_qkvg_proj_weight`) and the fused `[f_a | b]` gate projection (`_bfa_proj_weight`, padded to 8 rows), forked onto two streams for up to 128 rows. At decode sizes (M = 8 x batch rows) both GEMMs are tiny, so two launches plus the stream fork / join cost more than one GEMM with 144 more output rows.

Measured on Rubin single GPU, Kimi K3 KDA layer shapes per rank, own weights per layer, CUDA graph, µs per layer for the verify projection GEMMs, batch 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 / 16 (M = 8 x batch):

| | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 12 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| qkvg and [f_a \| b] (two GEMMs) | 15.6 | 15.7 | 17.7 | 15.2 | 19.7 | 17.0 | 18.2 | 18.5 |
| one stacked GEMM | 12.9 | 13.2 | 15.8 | 13.5 | 13.0 | 13.1 | 14.1 | 13.7 |

Proposal: in `finalize_decode_weights`, stack the two fused weights into one `[q | k | v | g | f_a | b | pad]` buffer and repoint `_qkvg_proj_weight`, `_bfa_proj_weight` and the per-projection weights to row views of it (no extra memory; prefill and decode GEMMs unchanged). The verify projection then runs one GEMM and takes qkvg and `[f_a | b]` as column views of its output; the verify kernel already reads the sections as strided views. Opt-in first via `TLLM_KDA_FUSE_VERIFY_PROJECTION=1`. PR to follow.

Related: #20174 routes `_project_gate_inputs` through the low-M dispatcher. The two compose (the stacked GEMM can go through the dispatcher too: 10.3–11.5 µs per layer at batch 1–4 in the same setup).

items.title: [Performance]: CuTe DSL MLA decode split-KV reduction is load-latency bound at small batch
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

The split-KV reduction of the CuTe DSL MLA decode kernels (`reduction_kernel` in `cute_dsl_kernels/blackwell/attention/mla/mla_decode_fp16.py` and `mla_decode_fp8.py`) accumulates the per-split partials one split at a time: each iteration issues a global load of `gAccO[i, ...]` and immediately consumes it, so with tens of splits the loop is load-latency bound. The runner also always launches it with one D band per row (`reducer_d_tiles = 1`), so at small batch (few rows) only a handful of CTAs run it.

Measured on Rubin single GPU (200-SM engineering sample), CUDA graph, Kimi K3 shapes (target FP8 KV, 12 heads, q = 8; drafter BF16, 8 heads, q = 7; batch 1, page 32), reduction time per call with the production split plan, current → prefetching loop with 4 D bands per row:

| KV (splits) | 2K (16) | 32K (64) | 128K (94) | 393K (100) | 1M (100) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 reduction µs | 5.10 → 4.00 | 10.79 → 4.95 | 14.63 → 6.43 | 15.73 → 6.91 | 8.47 → 2.88 |
| BF16 reduction µs | 4.83 → 3.73 | 10.73 → 4.98 | 14.95 → 5.95 | 15.45 → 6.77 | 15.30 → 6.66 |

Proposal: an optional prefetch in the reduction loop (load a group of 32 splits' partials into registers with a clamped split index, then accumulate them in split order with a mask, so every output element sees the same multiply-adds in the same order and the result is bitwise unchanged), and have the runner use 4 D bands per row while that grid fits a few SM waves. Opt-in first via `TLLM_CUTE_DSL_MLA_REDUCTION_PREFETCH=1`. End to end on Rubin, TP8 across 2 nodes (MNNVL), Kimi K3 with MTP decode, the decode step period dropped by 0.05 ms at 2K and 0.15–0.22 ms at 32K–393K context, with accepted tokens per step unchanged. PR to follow.

items.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1 CSA2: intermittent illegal address in the dynamic-token-sparse MLA generation kernel, which loads -1 index padding past the sparse length
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

- GPU: Vera Rubin, compute capability 10.7
- TensorRT-LLM main (CSA2 sparse backend code is byte-identical to main as of 2026-10-19), PyTorch backend
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, CSA2 sparse attention, FP8 KV

### Who can help?

@NVIDIA/trt-llm-torch-attention-devs

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Reproduction

With the CSA2 sparse backend, decode intermittently fails with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` (an illegal memory access). The error usually surfaces asynchronously in an unrelated later op (indexer, MoE launch, a cuBLAS GEMM). On the full model (TP4/EP4, CUDA graphs) about 40% of freshly started servers hit it within the first ~20 requests.

On a reduced-layer model (layers 0, 20, 21, 24 of the checkpoint; TP1, eager, block reuse off) it is deterministic: it fails on the first decode step of the first real request, 6/6 runs, also with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`. With launch blocking the error is returned by the launch itself (`AttentionOp::mlaGeneration` -> `launchFmhaKernel`):

- kernel: `fmhaSm107aKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16H512HVPerCta128PagedKvDenseDynamicTokenSparseP1MultiCtasKvGmemSepVarSeqQ64Kv128StaticKeepsAbForGen`
- CSA layer, generation, `num_tokens=1`, sparse top-k 640, grid (3,4,1), max KV length 640
- `sparse_attn_kv_lens` (the prepared lengths) = 78; `prepared_indices[:, :78]` are all valid and in range, `prepared_indices[:, 78:640]` are the `-1` padding written by the CSA2 staging step.

The same kernel passes in warmup (prepared length 2), and the non-multi-CTA variant used by the SWA layer just before passes.

### Expected behavior

Index slots past the per-token sparse length are ignored by the kernel (no loads issued for them), so the `-1` padding is never dereferenced.

### Actual behavior

The kernel issues KV loads for slots beyond the sparse length. The `-1` entries turn into addresses before the paged pool; whether that faults depends on what happens to be mapped there, which is why it is intermittent on the full model.

Evidence, same reduced model and prompts:

| variant | requests | illegal address |
|---|---|---|
| unchanged | first request of 6 runs | 6/6 |
| padding `-1` replaced by `0` before the FMHA call | 12 (async) + 12 (launch blocking) | 0 |
| same, plus 150 stress batches | 168 | 0 |

compute-sanitizer memcheck does not report it (TMA loads are not checked by default, and the allocation layout changes under the tool, so the fault disappears).

### Additional notes

Workaround in `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/sparse/csa2/backend.py`, `sparse_attn_predict`, before returning:

```python
metadata.prepared_indices[: metadata.num_tokens].clamp_(min=0)
```

This assumes the kernel masks the scores of slots past the sparse length, so pointing the padding at a valid row is numerically a no-op. We are verifying that bit-exactly at the op level and will report back here.

Suggested proper fix, kernel side: predicate (or clamp) the index and page loads for slots `>= ptrSparseMlaTopKLens[token]`, not only mask their scores. Alternatively, document that the padding must be a valid index and have CSA2 pad with a valid row while still masking by length.

Unrelated and benign, for completeness: `deep_gemm::sm100_sparse_mqa_logits` reads up to 16 B past the end of `sf_kv` by design ("Tail reads rely on PyTorch allocator padding"); it only shows up with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`.

items.title: [Perf]: DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram n-gram hash falls back to ~150 eager torch kernels per step with multiple tokens per request (speculative decoding)
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

- GPU: Vera Rubin, compute capability 10.7, single node, TP4/EP4
- TensorRT-LLM main (`tensorrt_llm/_torch/modules/engram/engram.py` unchanged on main since #19727), PyTorch backend, CUDA graphs
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` with speculative decoding (several tokens per request per step)

### Who can help?

@NVIDIA/trt-llm-torch-models-devs

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Reproduction

Serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with speculative decoding enabled and CUDA graphs on, run a single-request decode and profile it with nsys (`--cuda-graph-trace=node`).

### Expected behavior

The Engram n-gram hash computation for generation steps runs as a few fused launches, like the single-token decode fast path (`_compute_decode_hashes` -> `_decode_hash_kernel`).

### Actual behavior

`_compute_decode_hashes` returns `None` as soon as any request has more than one token in the forward:

```python
lengths = tuple(seq_lens_host[: len(request_ids)].tolist())
if any(length != 1 for length in lengths):
    return None
```

So every speculative generation step (draft tokens + verify, 6 tokens per request in our setup) falls back to the general torch path in `compute_hashes`. That path runs eagerly from the pre-replay hook (`refresh_captured_hashes`), outside the CUDA graph, and launches about 150 small kernels per step (`remainder` x48, `mul` x18, `bitwise_xor` x12, `bitwise_or` x8, stacks/copies), each a few µs but host-launch bound at ~7-8 µs apart.

Measured at batch 1, 32K context: the decode step period is 11.5 ms and the GPU is idle for 2.2 ms of it; about 1.4 ms of that idle time is this eager hash path. Without speculative decoding (1 token per request) the fast path is taken and the hash cost is negligible.

### Additional notes

The existing pieces almost cover the multi-token case. A prototype that keeps the current host-side bookkeeping, writes the forward's tokens into the history with one small Triton kernel and then calls the existing `_decode_hash_kernel` in `READ_CURRENT_HISTORY` mode per layer reduces the work to 3 launches + 1 H2D copy per step. It is bitwise identical to the torch path in our tests (hashes, history buffer, row mapping and cached outputs) for: seeded context chunks, 4 requests x 6 tokens padded to 32 with rollback to the accepted length, int32 inputs, out-of-range token ids, a context + generation mix, freed-and-reused rows. Duplicate request ids and token masks still take the torch path.

We are measuring the end-to-end gain and are happy to send this as a PR if the approach looks right.

items.title: [Bug]: fill_template.py fails with ValueError when a substitution value contains a colon
items.author: ShryukGrandhi
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

- CPU architecture: arm64 (also reproducible on x86_64; the script is pure Python)
- TensorRT-LLM branch: main (commit c6350002f)
- Python 3.12
- No GPU needed to reproduce

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [x] The official example scripts

### Reproduction

`triton_backend/tools/fill_template.py` says substitutions support escaping, but a value that contains a colon (escaped or not) crashes the script:

```bash
printf 'url: "${url}"\n' > config.pbtxt
python3 triton_backend/tools/fill_template.py config.pbtxt 'url:http\://localhost\:8000'
```

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "triton_backend/tools/fill_template.py", line 70, in <module>
    main(**vars(args))
  File "triton_backend/tools/fill_template.py", line 43, in main
    key, value = split(sub, ":")
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```

`main()` first runs `split(substitutions, ",")`, which already removes every backslash, and then runs `split(sub, ":")` on the result. By the time the second split runs, `\:` has turned into a plain `:`. So the value gets split again. The same double unescaping means a literal backslash in a value has to be written as four backslashes.

### Expected behavior

`url:http\://localhost\:8000` should produce `url: "http://localhost:8000"`. Only the first colon should separate the key from the value, so values such as URLs, `host:port` or Windows paths can be passed.

### actual behavior

The script exits with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` and the template is left unfilled.

### additional notes

Splitting each `key:value` pair on its first colon only (`sub.split(":", 1)`) fixes it.

items.title: [Bug]: etcd watch callback cancels discovery watch under asyncio debug mode
items.author: codebreaker77
items.body_excerpt:
On main `46d9966b54d9d11998b712e732fb20f64d4d35c0`, a real etcd notification can
cancel a live watch and leave its asyncio reader blocked when debug mode is
enabled. Re-requesting the same prefix returns the cached dead handle.

## Reproduction

With a dedicated etcd 3.5 server and a matching TensorRT-LLM Python environment:

```python
import asyncio
import uuid
from tensorrt_llm.serve.cluster_storage import Etcd3ClusterStorage

async def main():
    storage = Etcd3ClusterStorage("etcd://127.0.0.1:2379", "repro")
    prefix = "watch-repro/" + uuid.uuid4().hex + "/"
    watch = await storage.watch(prefix)
    pending = asyncio.create_task(watch.drain())
    await asyncio.sleep(0)  # reader waits before the SDK thread delivers
    assert await storage.set(prefix + "worker", "registered")
    print("key:", await storage.get(prefix + "worker"), flush=True)
    print(await pending, flush=True)

asyncio.run(main(), debug=True)
```

Run under an external process timeout: the failed wakeup can leave an orphaned
reader, so an asyncio timeout is not a sufficient whole-process safety bound.
Setting `debug=False` is the successful control.

## Observed

Three independent runs against real etcd all produced:

- Debug off: event delivered; SDK watch stays active.
- Debug on: logs `Non-thread-safe operation invoked on an event loop other than
  the current one`; no event delivered; key still readable; SDK watch removed.
- After recording failure and repairing the orphaned wakeup for test cleanup,
  disabling debug and calling `watch(prefix)` returns the same cached handle;
  a second etcd write produces no notification.

This could make a discovery consumer stop receiving worker changes. No router
state, model-serving traffic or GPU effects were measured. Production-mode
controls passed; the established runtime failure is under asyncio debug.

## Cause / proposed scope

`Etcd3WatchEventQueue.add_events_from_resp` mutates an asyncio queue directly on
the etcd SDK callback thread. Its later `call_soon_threadsafe(lambda: None)` is
too late to make that queue operation safe. The exception handler then cancels
the watch, while storage keeps its cached handle.

Capture the owning event loop and enqueue events on that loop using
`call_soon_threadsafe`, with focused threaded-delivery and pending-reader tests.
The unsafe pattern was already flagged in an old review:
https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/8210#discussion_r2415560025
I found no dedicated issue or current fix through searches for etcd/thread,
debug, watch/reconnect and the queue class name. This report adds runtime
evidence rather than claiming the pattern was previously unknown.

## Validation boundary

Real etcd-sdk-python 0.0.7 with Docker etcd 3.5.21. Full unchanged storage/logger
source modules loaded while bypassing TensorRT/native package initialization.
Windows Python 3.10 client with real-server I/O; supplementary actual-thread and
SDK-event checks also reproduce on Linux Python 3.12. The normal-package snippet
above and model serving were not executed locally. This is separate from the
expired-lease failure in #20529.

## Proposed patch and follow-up validation

A focused fix is available on [my fork](https://github.com/codebreaker77/TensorRT-LLM/tree/fix/20684-etcd-watch-threading),
commit [819f5c8f](https://github.com/codebreaker77/TensorRT-LLM/commit/819f5c8f).
It captures the owning event loop and schedules queue insertion onto that loop,
removing the private queue-loop wakeup. It does not include the separate lease
recovery work from #20529.

The nine new CPU cases produce 5 failures / 4 passes on unchanged source and
9 passes with the fix. The full existing storage suite plus these cases passes
62 tests on Linux Python 3.12. Six real-etcd runs with the fix (three each with
debug on/off) deliver two successive notifications and keep the watch active.
The same native-bootstrap isolation described above applies; no full-package,
model-serving or GPU validation is claimed. Applicable formatting/lint checks
pass. The branch is prepared for issue triage; no upstream PR has been opened.

items.title: CUTLASS 4.8.1
items.author: Junkai-Wu
items.body_excerpt:
### CuTe DSL * Bug fixes and improvements: - Fixed an issue with `cute.extern` where functions with zero arguments would generate invalid type signatures. Compiling such functions a second time would fail. - Clear error/warning are now emitted for `CopyUniversalOp` with memory attributes specified ([!3711](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/issues/3711)). - CUTLASS Primitives' `tensormap_replace` now keeps device-side TMA descriptor updates safe when a descriptor is shrunk below its original extent (e.g. grouped GEMM) and fixes a possible illegal memory access on Blackwell/Rubin. This behavior can be opted out by specifying `keep_oob_fetch_window=True`. See https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/tesla/tesla-release-notes-595-91-07/index.html#known-issues for more details on the known `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` bug. - Fixed unintended `sys.path` modification that could break imports in some environments where Torch was not installed e.g. JAX. * Known issues - Due to a bug in CTK, the use of some packed instructions result in invalid code generation. Given the nature of the instructions and how they are explicitly used, we have chosen to not silently rewrite these, but rather are flagging until the upstream compiler fixes are available. - Avoid packed higher-throughput FP8 (MMA_K=128) subtraction via inline PTX `sub.rn.e4m3x4.e4m3x4` or `sub.rn.e5m2x4.e5m2x4`, as incorrect code generation can produce wrong results. - Some CUTLASS Primitives packed mixed-input ops compile incorrectly on Rubin (sm107a/sm107f), resulting in wrong code generation. The specific patterns include: - Packed mul, sub, and add ops with bf16x2 or fp16x2 result type and f32x2 input type when result is converted to fp32 later. APIs affected: `add_packed_f16x2_f32x2_f32x2`, `add_packed_bf16x2_f32x2_f32x2`, `mul_packed_f16x2_f32x2_f32x2`, `mul_packed_bf16x2_f32x2_f32x2`, `sub_packed_f16x2_f32x2_f32x2`, `sub_packed_bf16x2_f32x2_f32x2` - For example: ``` x = prims.mul_packed_bf16x2_f32x2_f32x2(a, b) out[0], out[1] = f32(x[0]), f32(x[1]) # out[0], out[1] are wrong ``` - Packed mul op with bf16x2 or fp16x2 result type and mixed bf16x2 and fp16x2 input types when the first operand is a compilation-time constant. APIs affected: `mul_packed_bf16x2_bf16x2_f16x2`, `mul_packed_f16x2_f16x2_bf16x2` - For example: ``` x = prims.mul_packed_bf16x2_bf16x2_f16x2(2.0, b) # x is wrong x = prims.mul_packed_f16x2_f16x2_bf16x2(2.0, b) # x is wrong ``` * This release has been tested against the following packages: - FlashAttention: [main (1fc0221)](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/commit/1fc0221183e799363001394a12dd9e78e15f5dda) - Quack: [main (35266c32)](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/quack/commit/35266c3298f0e9bf6d5f46c30aace2eaeae517e3) - FlashInfer: [main (399b6c1)](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/399b6c1d31a13f38dd827018f89c6a04c8487acb) - cuDNN-Frontend: [deveop (986ef4d)](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/commit/986ef4d9078089ae9f0656dd65f15011309e4347) - Pytorch: [main (ca883d5)](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/commit/ca883d596dd5c0ce182976ed979d69d167ad706c) - TensorRT-LLM: [main (cc63e66)](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/commit/cc63e66daf52644f1441e117bb7ba67d20566016)
This discussion was created from the release CUTLASS 4.8.1.

items.title: CUDA SymmetricMemory: rank-local rendezvous failure leaves peer resources and stalls other ranks
items.author: jackLei0901
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

I tested the behavior when a CUDA SymmetricMemory rendezvous fails on a specific rank. By artificially injecting a peer-import or peer-map failure on Rank 0, Rank 1 returned after approximately 301 seconds, with the imported resources remaining unreleased. Although local tensor health checks passed on both ranks, the subsequent rendezvous operation within the same group failed during the metadata exchange phase. These results come from injected-fault testing, with one run per case, rather than the reproduction of a failure under a real-world workload.

#### AI-assisted technical report

AI assistance was used for the diagnostic and this report. Two processes shared one RTX 4090, using a Gloo group, the Store-exchange/POSIX-FD route, overlapping-device allowance and multicast disabled. The shim temporarily intercepts process-local DriverAPI calls; only rank 0's first peer import or map is failed.

H/R/M below denotes imported-handle references, address reservations and mappings remaining when the first call returned:

| Case | Rank 0 | Rank 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | Success | Success; fresh same-group second rendezvous and peer-data checks also passed on both ranks |
| Import failure | Error in 0.012 s; H/R/M 0/0/0; received FD still open | `RuntimeError("Wait timeout")` after 301 s; H/R/M 1/1/1 |
| Map failure | Error in 0.012 s; H/R/M 1/1/0; received FD still open | Same 301 s wait and H/R/M 1/1/1 |

The normal resources have committed owners; they are not leaks. Fault-case leftovers were measured while processes remained alive, before teardown. FD evidence is an open descriptor with matching identity at first return, not a complete close-call trace. The map case's rank-0 reservation leak is the already-known #201091 problem, not a new finding.

With injection disabled and fresh allocations, both fault-case retries failed in about 6 s: rank 0 waited for `CUDASymmetricMemory/1/1`, while rank 1 waited for `CUDASymmetricMemory/2/0`. Neither reached a new peer import. Both ranks observed metadata keys `0/0`, `0/1`, `1/0`, `2/1` present, with `1/1` and `2/0` absent. This corroborates exchange-sequence divergence; counters were not directly instrumented. Retry was a diagnostic, not an assertion that same-group recovery is currently supported.

The Store timeout was configured and read back as 5 s. The 301 s peer wait is consistent with the PrefixStore barrier's inherited timeout; that is a separate c10d concern, not the proposed fix here.

#### Source explanation

On the audited source, rank 0 throws inside the [peer-import loop](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/74b55cafb21cf7d14bf8adc466e256ef2b994533/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/CUDASymmetricMemory.cu#L1039) before reaching the [Store barrier](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/74b55cafb21cf7d14bf8adc466e256ef2b994533/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/CUDASymmetricMemory.cu#L1078). Rank 1 waits there. Peer [AllocationRef owners are constructed only afterward](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/74b55cafb21cf7d14bf8adc466e256ef2b994533/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/CUDASymmetricMemory.cu#L1121), leaving its imports and mappings without an owner when the barrier throws. Rank 0 also skips the barrier's exchange sequence, consistent with the divergent metadata keys observed on retry.

The diagnostic and sanitized evidence are linked below.

https://gist.github.com/jackLei0901/cf4c1ff43d39504291f084b4fc391975

#### Scope and limits

The tested library is a local build on reported pin `215856938cfe9347ea2d0a20a766577e45fa5bb8`, containing an earlier draft of #201091's local `alloc()` change. Its peer-rendezvous code, StoreExchange and Store code match `74b55cafb21cf7d14bf8adc466e256ef2b994533`; this is not a complete current-main build or the shared-helper revision in #201284.

No fix arm, two-physical-GPU run, NCCL process-group (`use_pg`) path, multicast, Fabric, ROCm, fatal CUDA error or process-loss case was tested. vLLM fallback relevance is source-based, not a serving reproduction.

#### Reporter conclusion and scope question

kapilsh, do you think it would be appropriate to use the existing `MulticastSetup` coordinated-outcome pattern to handle the subsequent processing for the peer setup phase? My goal is for the participating ranks to reach a consensus on success or failure, and—in the event of failure—to release the peer handles, mappings, and received file descriptors (FDs) they have acquired.

Should the agreed-upon behavior be limited strictly to "prompt coordinated failure handling and resource cleanup" (with the caller responsible for recreating the group or terminating the program), or should it also support "subsequent rendezvous within the same group"? This decision will determine the scope of the exchange sequence logic and the regression testing strategy. I haven't implemented the fix for coordinated failure handling yet; unless you need to support the "retry within the same group" feature, I plan to exclude it from the current implementation scope.

### Versions

PyTorch: 2.16.0a0+git2158569; reported pin: 215856938cfe9347ea2d0a20a766577e45fa5bb8.
CUDA build: 13.0; driver: 595.71.05; OS: Linux; GPU: one RTX 4090 shared by two processes.
Backend: CUDA SymmetricMemory; allocator: native, expandable segments disabled.

items.title: MPS backend hangs (uninterruptible sleep) after ~100-600s of sustained encoding on Apple Silicon
items.author: nicobrenner
items.body_excerpt:
## What happens

When running `SentenceTransformer.encode()` on the MPS device, the process silently freezes after about 100-600 seconds of cumulative GPU encoding. It enters uninterruptible sleep (U state at 0% CPU) and doesn't respond to SIGINT or SIGTERM, only `kill -9`.

This happens both across multiple encode() calls (cumulative time in one process) and during a single large encode() call if it needs more than ~100s of GPU time.

## Environment

- Apple M3 Max, 64 GB unified memory, 40-core GPU
- macOS 15.6.1 (Build 24G90)
- Python 3.12
- PyTorch 2.14.1
- SentenceTransformers (latest)
- Model: BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 (335M params)

```
$ python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.backends.mps.is_available()); print(torch.backends.mps.is_built())"
2.14.1
True
True
```

## Repro

```python
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
import time

model = SentenceTransformer("BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5", device="mps")

# enough text to sustain encoding for > 100s
texts = [f"This is sample text number {i} with some additional content to process." for i in range(50000)]

print("Starting encode...")
t0 = time.time()
# this will hang after ~100-600s of GPU encoding time
embeddings = model.encode(texts, batch_size=256, show_progress_bar=True)
print(f"Done in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s")
```

With `show_progress_bar=True` you can see it making progress before it freezes. No error, no exception, it just stops.

## What I see in ps

```
USER  PID  %CPU  STAT  TIME
nico  1234  0.0   U    3:43.68
```

The process is in U state (uninterruptible sleep, kernel-level wait) at 0% CPU. It accumulated ~3:43 of CPU time before hanging. Only `kill -9` works.

## What I've tried

1. **CPU instead of MPS** (`device="cpu"`): works reliably but ~10x slower
2. **Fresh subprocess per workload**: spawning a new Python process for each encoding batch resets the MPS state. Works for smaller workloads (<100s encoding each) but doesn't help if a single encode() call exceeds the threshold
3. Haven't tested `torch.mps.empty_cache()` between calls yet, might help if the root cause is memory pressure from MPSGraph caching

## Observations

- The hang correlates with cumulative GPU encoding time in the process, not with sample count
- Smaller datasets (1K-5K short texts) complete fine in fresh processes
- Larger datasets (50K texts) trigger the hang even in a fresh process during a single encode() call
- The threshold varies (100-600s), suggesting it depends on memory allocation patterns
- Memory usage grows steadily during normal operation before the hang (consistent with #154329)

## Possibly related

- #154329 (MPS memory leak, MPSGraph cache grows unboundedly). The unbounded memory growth could cause Metal command buffer submission to deadlock once memory pressure hits a threshold, which would explain the kernel-level uninterruptible sleep.

items.title: [MPS] F.interpolate (linear, bilinear, trilinear) returns the next input pixel at some output positions
items.author: tivris
items.body_excerpt:
Found while checking MPS ops against CPU on an M5. I have a fix with a regression test ready and can send a PR once this is marked actionable.

> The analysis and reproducer below were prepared with an AI assistant at my request; I reviewed and reran them.
>
> ### 🐛 Describe the bug
>
> On MPS, `F.interpolate` with `mode="linear"`, `"bilinear"` or `"trilinear"` returns the next input pixel at some output positions.
>
> ```python
> import torch
> import torch.nn.functional as F
>
> x = torch.arange(9.).view(1, 1, 9)
> for mode, inp in (("linear", x), ("bilinear", x.view(1, 1, 1, 9)), ("trilinear", x.view(1, 1, 1, 1, 9))):
>     size = (1,) * (inp.dim() - 3) + (29,)
>     cpu = F.interpolate(inp, size=size, mode=mode).flatten()
>     mps = F.interpolate(inp.to("mps"), size=size, mode=mode).cpu().flatten()
>     print(mode, cpu[14].item(), mps[14].item())
> ```
>
> ```
> linear 3.999999761581421 4.999999523162842
> bilinear 3.999999761581421 4.999999523162842
> trilinear 3.999999761581421 4.999999523162842
> ```
>
> Output 14 maps to source index `9 / 29 * 14.5 - 0.5 = 4`, so the expected value is `x[4] = 4`. The kernel computes it with a fused multiply-add, which gives `3.9999998`, one ulp below 4 (a separate float32 multiply and subtract give exactly 4). The kernels get the upper neighbour by adding 1 to the float index and truncating, e.g. `long3(n, c, real_x + 1)` in [`upsample_linear1d`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/c693e1ad4208dbe6fa705c481aa24ec3eb1758c7/aten/src/ATen/native/mps/kernels/UpSample.metal#L464). `3.9999998 + 1` rounds to `5.0`, so the kernel blends `x[3]` and `x[5]` with weight `0.9999998` on `x[5]`. [`upsample_bilinear2d`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/c693e1ad4208dbe6fa705c481aa24ec3eb1758c7/aten/src/ATen/native/mps/kernels/UpSample.metal#L503-L513), [`upsample_trilinear`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/c693e1ad4208dbe6fa705c481aa24ec3eb1758c7/aten/src/ATen/native/mps/kernels/UpSample.metal#L317-L371) and [`upsample_trilinear_backward`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/c693e1ad4208dbe6fa705c481aa24ec3eb1758c7/aten/src/ATen/native/mps/kernels/UpSample.metal#L415-L417) do the same. CPU ([`UpSample.h`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/c693e1ad4208dbe6fa705c481aa24ec3eb1758c7/aten/src/ATen/native/UpSample.h#L473-L475)) and CUDA add 1 to the truncated integer index instead.
>
> With `linear`, input sizes 2 to 64 and output sizes 2 to 300, 301 of 18,837 size pairs have a wrong output with `align_corners=False` and 136 with `align_corners=True`, and every wrong output sits at a source index, as the kernel computes it, one ulp below a power of two. `float16` and `bfloat16` are affected the same way. In 2D the error spans a whole output row or column, e.g. row and column 256 of a bilinear resize from `(65, 65)` to `(513, 513)`. The linear and bilinear backward use a separate gather kernel and match CPU, so forward and backward disagree at these positions. The trilinear backward adds gradient to the wrong input cell.
>

items.title: [RLlib] MultiAgentEnvRunner can downgrade WEIGHTS_SEQ_NO after rejecting stale module state
items.author: lindicaphxag-tech
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

`MultiAgentEnvRunner.set_state` uses `WEIGHTS_SEQ_NO` to reject stale positive-version module states, but **unconditionally assigns the incoming positive version to `self._weights_seq_no` even when the module weights were not applied**. A delayed older state therefore makes a runner's advertised version regress, despite its parameters remaining newer.

This is a separate, remaining EnvRunner-side version invariant from the learner-side correction in #67131; I have not mixed the two production patches.

## Deterministic counterexample using the current production method

Checked against the current `ray-project/ray` `master` implementation in `python/ray/rllib/env/multi_agent_env_runner.py`:

1. Runner is at `_weights_seq_no=8`, with policy parameters for version 8.
2. `set_state({COMPONENT_RL_MODULE: stale_v7_weights, WEIGHTS_SEQ_NO: 7})` is called (e.g. an explicit out-of-order state delivery).
3. The existing guard correctly **skips applying stale_v7_weights** (`8 < 7` is false).
4. However, the later `if weights_seq_no > 0: self._weights_seq_no = weights_seq_no` **downgrades the reported version from 8 to 7**.
5. Another version-8 delivery is now incorrectly considered new, triggering a redundant module update. External consumers observing the runner version see a version inconsistent with the current parameters.

A [source-extracted CPU regression with real production `Learner.set_state` and `MultiAgentEnvRunner.set_state` methods](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/blob/ci/rllib-learner-version-contract-20261022/ci/rllib_learner_weight_version_contract.py) reproduces the runner downgrade independently of #67131. The [passing GitHub Actions run](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/actions/runs/39810724497) records:

```
CONFIRMED SEPARATE DOWNSTREAM GAP: EnvRunner rejected stale parameters but downgraded its seq 8 -> 7
```

That fixture uses simple deterministic module objects (no live Ray actors); it proves the reachable method-level state transition, **not** that live Ray actor message reordering has been observed in a deployed workload. Stale explicit `set_state` and checkpoint ordering semantics should be discussed before changing behavior.

## Proposed narrowly scoped contract

For a positive `WEIGHTS_SEQ_NO`, `set_state` must never decrease a runner's version when it skips applying older parameters. A missing or zero version retains its documented force-apply behavior and must not advance the sequence without an agreed publication contract.

Potential minimal correction: only update `_weights_seq_no` when `weights_seq_no > self._weights_seq_no`, with a native `MultiAgentEnvRunner.set_state` test asserting weights and version remain coherent for stale / equal / newer values; include a forced module-only update case as a compatibility guard. A separate test should validate the exported `get_state` version.

## Scope and maintainer question

This is a focused state-provenance correctness case, not an assertion of RL training quality improvement, distributed linearizability, or a measured production incident. It is related to but separate from #67131 (which addresses `Learner.set_state`); the best separation is probably to finish #67131 without expanding its diff, then patch `MultiAgentEnvRunner` in a small independent PR.

Would maintainers prefer this as a separate narrow PR, or combined with the existing weight-sequence discussion? I can prepare a native test and minimal implementation once the intended semantics are confirmed.

AI assistance was used for the source audit and deterministic harness. All claims above are limited to the actual code and observed Actions logs.


### Minimal candidate and completed red/green validation — 2026-10-22

A targeted **two-file** solution is now ready on my fork, based directly on current official `master@a82c56e`: [compare only the candidate implementation and native tests](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/compare/a82c56ee769fc02b1e4442d2ade57c9713263443...fix/rllib-envrunner-monotonic-seq-20261022). Production diff: **2 lines inserted / 2 deleted** in `multi_agent_env_runner.py`; native test: 42 lines. It preserves the existing force-update behavior for missing/zero `WEIGHTS_SEQ_NO` and the newer-version path. No broader API or learner changes.

The independent [CPU source-extracted red/green GitHub Actions run **completed successfully**](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/actions/runs/39811945539). It executes the actual `MultiAgentEnvRunner.set_state` body from both the patch and pinned unchanged official source. It confirms:
- Original: stale v7 payload rejected by runner at v8, yet version **8 → 7**; subsequent already-resident v8 is unnecessarily applied again.
- Proposed: stale v7 is rejected **without** downgrade; equal v8 is a no-op; newer v9 updates module/version together; unversioned module-only state still force-applies without incrementing the global version.
- Candidate production/native-test source compilation and focused static checks pass. Full native Ray runtime and multi-actor CI **not yet run**; this is not a claim of deployed message reordering.

[Scoped fork CI PR #5](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/pull/5) contains independent verification scripts/workflow **only**, excluded from the proposed upstream diff. To keep existing [Learner-side PR #67131](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/67131) reviewable, I propose handling this EnvRunner-side guarantee in a separate minimal PR once a maintainer agrees with the intended version semantics.

items.title: [RLlib] Learner state restore can mix optimizer provenance or publish unseen weights
items.author: lindicaphxag-tech
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

I found two related **causal state-publication** problems in the current `Learner.set_state` implementation:

1. For a versioned state containing **both RLModule weights and optimizer state**, the module can be rejected because its version is old **or equal**, while the corresponding optimizer state is still applied. Equal update counters are not globally unique identities: two different Learners can perform ten Adam updates on different data, ending at the same version with different parameters and moments.
2. `Learner.get_state(components=COMPONENT_OPTIMIZER)` can return a **versioned optimizer-only packet**. When `Learner.set_state` receives such a packet with a newer version, it currently updates its own `WEIGHTS_SEQ_NO` without installing any module weights. A later, genuinely updated module with the same version can then be rejected.

These concern two independent invariants: **paired component admission** and **causal weight-version publication**.

### Actual production-source and real Adam counterexamples

[Production-source red/green regression CI](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/actions/runs/39903883741) executes the checkout's actual `Learner.set_state` function with real `torch.optim.Adam`, and pins the unchanged existing #67131 head as the baseline.

| Scenario | Unmodified next-step / behavior | Minimal candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Live module v10 receives paired snapshot v9 | Incorrect old Adam state loaded; next-step L2 drift **0.000322280417** | Paired state rejected; L2 drift **0** |
| Two independent Adam histories share v10 | Incoming module rejected but unrelated optimizer moments loaded; next-step L2 drift **0.051059705430** | Entire equal-version pair rejected; L2 drift **0** |
| Optimizer-only v11 arrives before module v11 | Weight version falsely advances to v11; actual later weights are refused | Version remains v10 until genuine module v11 is installed |

The method was additionally tested in a **real Ray 2.59.0 Learner/torch runtime**, using the exact current production method against the pinned unmodified source on the same wheel. The [native-runtime red/green CI](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/actions/runs/39905482088) passed: old/equal paired rejection, optimizer-only version isolation, actual installation of next-version module tensors, and newer paired recovery.

### Narrow review candidate (only two files)

[Review-focused production + native-test diff](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/compare/fix/rllib-version-unversioned-set-state-20261018...review/rllib-causal-paired-state-minimal-20261023)

- Production code: add an optimizer guard only when a **paired, positively versioned** module state is refused by the existing strict-newer module predicate; publish a new weight sequence only when a module-state component was actually supplied and accepted.
- Native `test_learner.py`: three focused tests for stale paired, equal paired and optimizer-only future-version cases.
- Preserve unversioned module updates, optimizer-only independent restores and newer paired restores.

**Semantics question for maintainers:** When a *complete, versioned* snapshot has a version equal to the current Learner, should it (a) be a no-op for both model and optimizer, consistent with today's strict-newer module rule, or (b) explicitly restore **both** components as an authoritative checkpoint? The candidate implements (a), but either policy must avoid partially applying the paired state.

This is **paired admission consistency, not ACID transactionality**: the minimal guard does not roll back a module installation if a subsequent optimizer setter raises. Source-driven tests and Ray 2.59 runtime checks are not a complete current-master multi-actor test run. No RL return gain or novel optimizer algorithm is claimed.

The previously open [#67131](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/67131) addresses the related monotonic version issue and remains unchanged. Please confirm the intended checkpoint semantics before I send a separate minimal upstream PR or modify its scope. The detailed causal model and limitations are in the [research note](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/blob/research/rllib-stale-optimizer-transaction-20261023/research/RLLIB_CAUSAL_VERSIONED_STATE_20261023.md).

**Independent official-master reproduction (2026-10-23):**
The equal-version foreign-Adam collision and optimizer-only phantom weight
publication have now also been reproduced against the **unchanged official
Ray master commit `fbd093c05644bc3ba1429eef1188ec85ea563158`**, using
the same source-derived real-Adam fixtures, not just the existing #67131
head. [Passing source-pinned official-master CI](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/actions/runs/39905764492).
The corresponding patched-vs-original runtime smoke with a real Ray 2.59
Learner and changed module tensors passed:
[real Learner red/green](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/actions/runs/39905482088).
The minimal production-and-native-tests candidate remains only **two files**
relative to the existing #67131 branch; no official new PR has been opened.

items.title: [Data] Terminal-only waits are counted as task output backpressure
items.author: Yin-1022
items.body_excerpt:
## Problem / Description

While reviewing #67180, I noticed a separate, pre-existing issue in DataOpTask's output-backpressure accounting.

`DataOpTask._track_task_`output_backpressure() currently starts the output-backpressure timer whenever `max_bytes_to_read == 0`. 
However, a zero read budget does not necessarily mean that the task has unread output.

For example, an empty streaming task can already have its stream fully exhausted, with no block or metadata output left to consume, while the driver is only waiting to observe terminal completion. 
If on_data_ready() is called with a zero output-read budget during this period, the task still accumulates task_output_backpressure_s.

This means time spent waiting only for terminal confirmation can be reported as output backpressure even though no output is waiting to be read.

This issue is separate from #67180 and reproduces on the unmodified current implementation.

## Minimal Reproduction
A minimal internal-API regression case is:

```
streaming_gen = create_stub_streaming_gen(block_nbytes=[])

task = DataOpTask(
    0,
    streaming_gen,
    BlockRefCounter(),
    "test_op",
)

ray.get(streaming_gen.completed(), timeout=20)
assert streaming_gen._stream_exhausted()

clock = [100.0]
monkeypatch.setattr(
    "ray.data._internal.execution.interfaces.physical_operator.time.perf_counter",
    lambda: clock[0],
)

fetcher = InlineMetadataFetcher()

# No output exists; only terminal completion remains.
assert task.on_data_ready(0, fetcher) == 0

clock[0] += 10

# Allow the current implementation to observe EOF and finish.
assert task.on_data_ready(1, fetcher) == 0

assert task.has_finished
assert task._total_output_backpressure_s == 0
```

### Actual behavior (unmodified Ray):
```
task._total_output_backpressure_s == 10.0
```

The task reports 10 seconds of output backpressure even though the streaming generator produced no output.

### Expected behavior:
```
task._total_output_backpressure_s == 0
```

Waiting only for terminal completion should not count as output backpressure when there is no unread block or metadata output.

Actual unread output should continue to count normally, including the case where the generator stream is already exhausted but a block/metadata pair has already been pulled and remains pending inside DataOpTask.

## Proposal

Track output backpressure only when both conditions are true:

1. max_bytes_to_read == 0
2. the task still has unread output.

A task still has unread output when at least one of the following holds:

1. _pending_block_ref is non-ni;
2. _pending_meta_ref is non-nil
3. the streaming generator has not yet been exhausted.

If a backpressure interval is already open and these conditions stop being true, close the interval even if the output-read budget remains zero. 
This prevents terminal-only waiting time from being included in the metric while preserving accounting for actual pending output.

items.title: [RLlib] Restored multi-agent EnvRunner retains stale routing after weights recover
items.author: lindicaphxag-tech
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

On the new RLlib stack, `Algorithm.restore_env_runners` correctly reconstructs modules and copies RLModule weights/version/connector state from the healthy local EnvRunner into a restored remote EnvRunner. **It does not restore the local EnvRunner's runtime-modified `policy_mapping_fn` or `policies_to_train`.** Those values are not serialized in `MultiAgentEnvRunner.get_state()`, so recovery can yield the *new correct weights with the old policy routing/training selection*.

This is especially relevant for dynamic multi-agent leagues, which update `env_runner.config.multi_agent(policy_mapping_fn=..., policies_to_train=...)` after adding/cloning policies. This is a **distinct recovery-consistency issue** from #67103's intra-runner weight-installation-before-mapping guarantee and from #67284's version monotonicity issue.

### Production mechanism

- `MultiAgentEnvRunner.get_state()` returns RLModule weights, `WEIGHTS_SEQ_NO`, connector state and sampled-step counters, but no runtime multi-agent mapping or trainability selectors.
- `Algorithm.restore_env_runners()` reconstructs modules from `MultiRLModuleSpec.from_module(from_env_runner.module)`, then invokes `er.set_state(ray.get(state_ref))` on restored actors. It does not copy `from_env_runner.config.policy_mapping_fn` or `policies_to_train`.
- `Algorithm.add_module()` changes the AlgorithmConfig only when passed `new_agent_to_module_mapping_fn` / `new_should_module_be_updated`; callbacks that update EnvRunner config directly can leave the original construction config behind. Restored workers cannot rely solely on default constructor configuration to recover dynamic mapping.

### Exact deterministic counterexample, with actual Ray Actor RPC

1. Local source EnvRunner now has modules `main=42` and `league_1=17`, weight sequence v5, mapping `league_1`, trainable set `{main,league_1}`.
2. A freshly constructed remote Ray Actor has only `main=-7`, seq v0, original mapping `main`, trainable set `{main}`.
3. Run the **actual extracted production** `Algorithm.restore_env_runners`, `MultiAgentEnvRunner.get_state`, `set_state` methods through a real `FaultTolerantActorManager` and `EnvRunnerGroup.foreach_env_runner`. The "restored" Actor is explicitly recreated in the test; no process crash is claimed.
4. **Official unchanged source**: remote Actor has correct modules/weights `42,17` and seq `5`, **but still routes to `main`** and trains only `main`.
5. **Minimal candidate**: capture the local source's mapping and trainable set alongside the weight state, and install them on the *same restored actor after* its weights: final mapping `league_1`, trainable set `{main,league_1}`.

[Real Ray Actor red/green GitHub Actions — **success**](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/actions/runs/39904779455); [source-method red/green — **success**](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/actions/runs/39904518727).

The complete fork-only test and workflow are on [fork PR #8](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/pull/8). The separate [production-only candidate](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/compare/7795d644673b4a4ed4d407fd9e7b0ca981e9606b...fix/rllib-restored-runner-dynamic-policy-config-20261023) changes only `python/ray/rllib/algorithms/algorithm.py`, without changing the existing upstream #67103 head.

### Proposed recovery contract and boundaries

When restoring with a **local source EnvRunner**, replicate the coherent tuple `(module specification, module weights, weight version, policy_mapping_fn, policies_to_train)`. Install the module and state *before* enabling its matching routing selector on that same actor.

This is **not** a linearizable cross-cluster activation protocol, does not yet address recovery when no local source EnvRunner exists, and is **not** a full native same-commit Ray 3.0 integration test. Actual actor-RPC tests used the released compiled Ray 2.59.0 wheel plus the current production method bodies; policy modules are small deterministic scalar state objects.

**Maintainer question:** Is a recovery-specific copy of the current local EnvRunner policy mapping and training selector desirable in the generic `Algorithm.restore_env_runners` path, or should this information be formalized as part of a dedicated (versioned) multi-agent runtime configuration checkpoint? I can prepare a targeted native Ray test for whichever contract is intended, keeping #67103 focused.

AI tooling assisted the audit and deterministic harness; the scope/limitations above are based on the actual code and successful Actions logs.

### Native regression candidate and repeated complete CI (2026-10-23)

Added a focused native `TestAlgorithm.test_restore_env_runner_reinstates_runtime_multi_agent_routing` case in the *fork-only candidate* `python/ray/rllib/algorithms/tests/test_algorithm.py`. It calls the production `Algorithm.restore_env_runners` method, checks the missing module is reconstructed, confirms module state installation precedes updated `policy_mapping_fn` and `policies_to_train`, and checks the restoration counter.

Current candidate consists of just [**two upstream files**](https://github.com/lindicaphxag-tech/ray/compare/7795d644673b4a4ed4d407fd9e7b0ca981e9606b...fix/rllib-restored-runner-dynamic-policy-config-20261023): the Algorithm restoration method and that native test. items.title: [RFC]: Support asynchronous video generation in the Batch API
items.author: scarlet25151
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

Add `/v1/videos` as a Batch endpoint. Clients submit OpenAI-style Batch JSONL, and the Batch worker creates each video job, waits for its terminal status, and saves the generated content to AIBrix file storage before reporting the row as completed.

The first backend protocol is vLLM-Omni's Videos API. MiniMax-H3 reference-conditioned generation is a motivating workload; model-specific parameters remain request data. The implementation reuses Batch dispatch, concurrency, progress tracking, and storage, together with the gateway's existing asynchronous-job routing.

### Motivation

AIBrix already supports individual asynchronous video jobs, but its Batch execution path expects a single JSON request followed by a final JSON response. A video job has a different lifecycle: creation returns an ID, generation continues in the backend, and the content is downloaded separately. Treating the create response as the completed Batch result would finish rows before generation succeeds and release concurrency slots while work is still queued.

Users running offline video datasets need the existing Batch capabilities: JSONL input, bounded concurrency, per-row results and errors, interruption recovery, and output retrieval after worker resources have been released. A backend-local video ID alone is insufficient when the Batch runtime owns and later removes the generating Pod.

This proposal follows [RFC #2674](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/issues/2674) and its merged implementation, [PR #2740](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/pull/2740). That work supplies public job identity, ownership, persistence, and Pod routing. This RFC adds a Batch consumer of that API. The backend remains authoritative for video status and content; the gateway registry remains a routing catalog.

[RFC #1595](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/issues/1595) discusses an xDiT generation API, and [RFC #1966](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/issues/1966) discusses broader multimodal serving. This proposal is limited to executing Videos API requests through Batch.

### Proposed Change

Extend the existing Batch request lifecycle so one video row includes creation, polling, content persistence, and result writing. Keep protocol handling in the Batch client and bind Batch storage and progress operations from the job driver.

#### 1. Input contract

Accept `endpoint: "/v1/videos"` when creating a Batch. Each input line retains the existing `custom_id`, `method`, `url`, and `body` envelope. Require `POST`, a model, and a string prompt for this endpoint.

Example input line, expanded for readability:

```json
{
  "custom_id": "video-001",
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "/v1/videos",
  "body": {
    "model": "minimax-h3",
    "prompt": "Continue the motion shown in the reference clip.",
    "video_reference": {
      "video_url": "https://media.example.com/reference.mp4"
    },
    "num_inference_steps": 50,
    "flow_shift": 12.0,
    "extra_params": {
      "task": "ref2va",
      "duration": 4.0,
      "audio_flow_shift": 3.0
    }
  }
}
```

The URL above is illustrative. Actual inputs may use backend-accessible URLs or supported data URLs. Images use `image_reference.image_url`. Reference objects or lists retain the shape supported by the selected backend version.

The Batch client converts the JSON body into `multipart/form-data`, as required by vLLM-Omni:

| JSONL value | Wire representation |
| --- | --- |
| Scalar parameters, such as `prompt`, `model`, or `num_inference_steps` | Corresponding text form field |
| `image_reference`, `video_reference`, and `audio_reference` | JSON-encoded form field |
| `extra_params` and other supported JSON-valued parameters | JSON-encoded form field |

The compatibility target is the Batch envelope and Videos endpoint lifecycle. The reference fields and `extra_params` are vLLM-Omni extensions, not a promise that every body is accepted by OpenAI or another backend. The first implementation supports JSON-representable inputs; resolving uploaded file IDs or worker-local file paths into multipart uploads is outside its scope.

Existing chat JSONL is not reinterpreted by model name. A user migrating a dataset must explicitly convert its text and media fields into a Videos body. The worker does not infer `task`, generation parameters, or media semantics from `minimax-h3`.

#### 2. Execution and completion

The normal, validated Batch path already counts input rows and dispatches them concurrently:

```text
MDS validation -> job driver -> runtime connection -> DispatchEngine
-> Channel.send -> output/error JSONL -> request counts
```

Add the following Videos execution branch:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Read a validated Batch row"] --> B["Acquire a dispatch slot and select a channel"]
    B --> C{"Saved execution handle?"}
    C -->|No| D["Convert JSON to multipart and POST /v1/videos"]
    D --> E["Save the returned video ID and destination"]
    C -->|Yes| F["Resume the original video job"]
    E --> F
    F --> G["GET status asynchronously"]
    G -->|queued / in_progress| G
    G -->|completed| H["GET content and persist the video"]
    G -->|failed| I["Return a row error"]
    H --> J["Return final Video metadata and file ID"]
    I --> K["Write result or error JSONL"]
    J --> K
    K --> L["Update request counts and release the slot"]
```

`queued` and `in_progress` are intermediate states. A successful row requires the video file and its output JSONL record to be saved. A backend failure or a terminal polling/content error uses the existing Batch row-error path. Output-persistence failures retain the execution record for the existing deferred/recovery path.

The serial path for inputs whose total is not yet known should call the same video executor. This proposal does not change that cursor protocol.

#### 3. Routing and recovery

When using the gateway, the worker stores the returned public video ID and uses the same gateway and identity for status, cont

items.title: Runtime fails to launch an s3:// model: the downloaded path is a Path, and the launch log line raises TypeError
items.author: wguo7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`SubprocessEngineLauncher.launch()` gets the model path from `_resolve_model_path()` ([model_runtime.py#L898](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix/aibrix/runtime/model_runtime.py#L898)). For an `s3://` or `tos://` artifact, that function returns whatever `download_model()` returns ([model_runtime.py#L1022](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix/aibrix/runtime/model_runtime.py#L1022)). The downloader returns a `pathlib.Path` ([base.py#L254](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix/aibrix/downloader/base.py#L254) and [base.py#L276](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix/aibrix/downloader/base.py#L276)), even though `_resolve_model_path()` is annotated `-> str`.

The `Path` goes into `cmd` after `--model` (or `--model-path` for SGLang). Before `Popen`, the launcher logs the command with `" ".join(cmd)` ([model_runtime.py#L939-L945](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix/aibrix/runtime/model_runtime.py#L939-L945)), and `str.join` raises `TypeError: sequence item 4: expected str instance, PosixPath found` (item 4 is the model path in the vLLM command). As a result, the weights are downloaded and the engine is never started. From reading the code, `activate()` then removes the model and re-raises ([model_runtime.py#L1781-L1789](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix/aibrix/runtime/model_runtime.py#L1781-L1789)). The restart path calls the same launcher ([model_runtime.py#L1653-L1663](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/f3300be0e65f81760ec3b0287aebbf1b638a4d1a/python/aibrix/aibrix/runtime/model_runtime.py#L1653-L1663)), so it should fail the same way. The repro below calls `launch()` directly with S3. I did not run `activate()` or a restart. TOS goes through the same `BaseDownloader.download_model()`, which returns the same `Path`, but I did not run a TOS repro.

Local paths and `hf://` or `huggingface://` URLs are returned as strings, so they are not affected. The existing test `test_resolve_model_path_returns_the_downloaded_path` replaces `download_model` with a function that returns a `str`, so it does not catch this.

### Steps to Reproduce

The script stores one file under `s3://bkt/models/qwen3-0.6b` in an in-process S3 (moto), replaces `subprocess.Popen`, and calls `SubprocessEngineLauncher.launch()` with that URL. No engine and no network are used. Output on main (f3300be):

```
resolved model path type: PosixPath
launch raised: TypeError sequence item 4: expected str instance, PosixPath found
engine process started: False
expected: launch returns the pid and starts the engine with --model <local dir>/...
```

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Run: PYTHONPATH=<aibrix>/python/aibrix python repro.py

SubprocessEngineLauncher.launch() with an s3:// artifact. _resolve_model_path()
returns the downloader's pathlib.Path, and the launch log line
" ".join(cmd) raises TypeError, so the engine is never started.

S3 is simulated in-process with moto, and subprocess.Popen is replaced so no
engine is started.
"""

import logging
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile

os.environ["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"] = "us-east-1"
os.environ["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] = "testing"
os.environ["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] = "testing"
local_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.environ["DOWNLOADER_LOCAL_DIR"] = local_dir + "/"

import boto3  # noqa: E402
from moto import mock_aws  # noqa: E402

from aibrix.runtime import model_runtime as mr  # noqa: E402

logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)  # keep the downloader's logs out of the output

popen_calls = []


class FakePopen:
    def __init__(self, cmd, **kwargs):
        popen_calls.append(cmd)
        self.pid = 4242


subprocess.Popen = FakePopen

with mock_aws():
    s3 = boto3.client("s3", region_name="us-east-1")
    s3.create_bucket(Bucket="bkt")
    s3.put_object(Bucket="bkt", Key="models/qwen3-0.6b/config.json", Body=b"{}")

    resolved = mr._resolve_model_path("s3://bkt/models/qwen3-0.6b")
    print("resolved model path type:", type(resolved).__name__)

    inst = mr.ModelInstance(model_name="qwen3-0.6b", port=18001, ipc_name="kvc_qwen3")
    try:
        pid = mr.SubprocessEngineLauncher().launch(
            inst, "s3://bkt/models/qwen3-0.6b", engine_config=None, additional_config=None
        )
        cmd = popen_calls[0]
        model_arg = cmd[cmd.index("--model") + 1].replace(local_dir, "<local dir>")
        print(f"launch ok, pid {pid}, --model {model_arg}")
    except Exception as e:
        print("launch raised:", type(e).__name__, e)
    print("engine process started:", bool(popen_calls))
    print(
        "expected: launch returns the pid and starts the engine with --model <local dir>/..."
    )
```

</details>

### Expected behavior

`launch()` starts the engine with `--model <local dir>/qwen3-0.6b`, the same as for a local path. `_resolve_model_path()` returns a `str`, as its annotation says.

### Environment

- AIBrix version: main at f3300be
- Deployment environment: none. The repro runs the launcher in-process with moto for S3 (macOS arm64, Python 3.12.15)
- LLM(s) being used: none (only a placeholder `config.json` is downloaded)

### Area

Runtime

I have a fix with a test ready and will open a PR.
